signature.name: Narikala Fortress
signature.detail: The ancient hilltop citadel is Tbilisi's defining sight, with sweeping views over the Old Town and river. Go in late afternoon for cooler air and sunset light; walk up from the Old Town or take the cable car.

signature.name: Old Tbilisi
signature.detail: The maze of lanes, balconies and bathhouses is the city's historic heart and best explored on foot. Start early to avoid crowds and wear comfortable shoes for the cobbled, hilly streets.

signature.name: Holy Trinity Cathedral of Tbilisi
signature.detail: One of the largest Orthodox cathedrals in the world, it dominates the skyline and is a must for its scale and frescoes. Dress modestly (cover shoulders and knees) and visit outside service times for quiet viewing.

signature.name: Bridge of Peace
signature.detail: The glass-and-steel pedestrian bridge is a modern icon linking the Old Town with Rike Park. Visit at dusk when the LED lights switch on; it is a short walk from the sulfur baths.

signature.name: Chronicles of Georgia
signature.detail: This monumental colonnade of carved pillars tells Georgia's history and offers wide views over the city and sea. It is a bit out of the centre, so take a taxi and go in the morning for soft light.

signature.name: Tbilisi Sulfur Baths
signature.detail: The domed bathhouses in Abanotubani are where the city's name comes from and a classic Tbilisi experience. Book a private room in advance and bring a towel; evenings are busiest.

signature.name: Metekhi Church
signature.detail: Perched on a cliff above the Kura River, this historic church frames one of the city's most photographed views. Combine it with a walk through the Old Town and cross the nearby Bridge of Peace.

signature.name: Mtatsminda Park
signature.detail: A hilltop amusement park reached by a funicular, with panoramic views and a giant Ferris wheel. Ride up in the late afternoon and stay for sunset over the city.
